data.raw_text:
No one told me freelancing could turn into this.
I hired a global team, built systems, and scaled fast.

I had no idea it would turn into a full-fledged agency. I didn’t anticipate hiring team members, managing clients, building systems, and working with people around the world.

Here are five things I wish I had known earlier:

1. Scope creep is common - and sometimes fine if it builds trust. But set limits. If you’re not tracking it, it snowballs fast. Be generous, but don’t let yourself be taken advantage of.

2. SOPs unlock speed - they allow you to hire faster and train better. I record Loom videos of tasks and feed them into AI to write the steps. It’s how I scale smartly.

3. Hire slowly, fire fast - you can find top-tier talent anywhere. I’ve discovered amazing people in the Philippines and Latin America who are now integral to our team.

4. Talk about money early - falling behind on invoicing or collections leads to bigger problems down the road. Cash flow is king when you’re paying others to get work done.

5. Other freelancers and agencies are not your competition - they’re your network. They’ll refer work to you, help with overflow, and keep you sharp.

If you’re growing from solo to agency, learn from the chaos I went through. PS that’s my studio office that I try to go to more often!

What’s one thing you wish someone told you when you started building a team?
